open_points.subject: Issuing credentials for a revoked viewer
open_points.text: M01 says `active → revoked` is terminal and revocation invalidates all viewer credentials, while M02 says only that credentials are issued, re-issued, and revoked by an administrator; it does not say whether issuance is allowed after the viewer is revoked.
open_points.question: May an administrator issue or re-issue a ViewerAccessCredential for a revoked ClientViewer?
options: Reject issuance because viewer revocation is terminal
Create a non-revoked credential that remains unusable while the viewer is revoked
open_points.default_guess: Reject issuance for a revoked viewer.

witness.initial: Viewer V is revoked and all of V's old credentials and sessions have been revoked.
events: An administrator requests a new access link for V.
outcomes: The request is rejected because a revoked viewer cannot receive credentials.
A fresh ViewerAccessCredential is created, but entry cannot create an active session because V remains revoked.
witness.observer: The administrator sees either a rejection or a new one-time access secret.

open_points.subject: Creating a project grant for a revoked viewer
open_points.text: M04 says a ProjectViewerGrant is created by an administrator and validates the project lifecycle elsewhere, but it does not say whether the target ClientViewer must be active; M01 makes viewer revocation terminal.
open_points.question: May a new ProjectViewerGrant be created for a revoked ClientViewer?
options: Require the target viewer to be active
Allow the grant record to be created even though the revoked viewer cannot use it

witness.initial: Viewer V is revoked; active Registry project P has never been granted to V.
events: An administrator grants P to V.
outcomes: No grant is created because V is revoked.
An active ProjectViewerGrant is created but remains unusable because V cannot authenticate.
witness.observer: The administrator sees either a rejection or a persisted grant in access-management reads and audit.

open_points.subject: Producer grants for an all-projects principal
open_points.text: M13 says an `all_projects` principal admits imports without consulting grants, while M15 says ProducerProjectGrant is `consulted only when the principal's scope_mode is granted_projects`; neither passage says whether the grant-creation action refuses an `all_projects` principal or creates an inert grant.
open_points.question: Can an administrator create a ProducerProjectGrant for a ServicePrincipal whose scope_mode is `all_projects`?
options: Reject it because grants are valid only for `granted_projects` principals
Create and retain the grant even though authorization never consults it

witness.initial: Active service principal S has `scope_mode = all_projects`; Registry project P is active.
events: An administrator requests a producer grant from S to P.
outcomes: The request is rejected and no ProducerProjectGrant exists.
A ProducerProjectGrant is created and audited, but has no authorization effect.
witness.observer: The administrator sees different command results and persisted producer-grant data.

open_points.subject: Allocations missing from an imported version during activation
open_points.text: The section first says that on activation, sections absent from the new version leave allocations that `become unresolved against the active version`, but later says `activation of a version is refused while any section allocation would be unresolved against it`.
open_points.question: When a candidate imported version omits a section targeted by an existing allocation, does activation succeed and expose an unresolved allocation, or is activation refused until re-allocation?
options: Activate and retain the allocation as unresolved against the new active version
Refuse activation until all such allocations are re-allocated
open_points.default_guess: Refuse activation until the allocations are resolved.

witness.initial: Version V1 is active and expense E has an allocation to section A; candidate version V2 has no plan for A.
events: An operator attempts to activate V2 without re-allocating E.
outcomes: V2 becomes active and E's allocation is reported as unresolved.
Activation is refused; V1 remains active.
witness.observer: The operator sees success versus refusal, and viewers may see either V2 with unresolved data or the unchanged V1 budget.

open_points.subject: Identity of SectionProgress
open_points.text: M32 calls SectionProgress a persisted entity and gives fields `project_id` and `section_id (unique)`, but supplies no `progress_id` and never states whether its identity is `section_id`, `(project_id, section_id)`, or a separate portal-minted identifier.
open_points.question: What is the identity of a SectionProgress entity, and what identifier names it in repositories, references, and audit records?
options: The globally unique `section_id` is also the SectionProgress identity
The composite `(project_id, section_id)` is its identity
The portal mints a separate `progress_id`
open_points.default_guess: Use `section_id` as the SectionProgress identity because the text declares it unique and specifies one row per section.

witness.initial: Section S in project P has no progress record.
events: A staff member records progress for S for the first time.
The progress update is audited or later addressed for another update.
outcomes: The record and audit are named by S's `section_id` or the `(P,S)` composite.
A fresh portal UUID identifies the progress entity independently of S.
witness.observer: Repository, audit, and later API implementers see incompatible identifiers for the same entity.

open_points.subject: Eligibility to create or update SectionProgress
open_points.text: M32 says `only sections with planned work in the active version participate in derived progress`, but does not say whether `set_section_progress` may create or update a record for a same-project section that is absent from the active version or has zero planned work.
open_points.question: Must a section currently have positive planned work in the active budget version before staff may create or update its SectionProgress?
options: Allow progress for any same-project PortalSection and ignore it in derived progress until it has active planned work
Reject the update unless the section has planned work in the active version
open_points.default_guess: Allow it for any same-project section, because progress is attached to the stable PortalSection across version changes.

witness.initial: Project P has active budget V; stable section S exists but has no plan in V.
events: Authorized staff sets S to 40% completion.
A later budget version containing S with planned work is activated.
outcomes: The update is stored and the later version immediately derives 40% for S.
The update is rejected, so the later version has no recorded progress for S.
witness.observer: Staff sees acceptance versus rejection, and later viewers see different progress after S returns to the active budget.

open_points.subject: Replay of a progress-photo intake with changed content
open_points.text: M35 says `replay of one intake_id never duplicates`, but unlike Expense and WorkPayment it does not say whether the same `intake_id` with different file, project, date, section, caption, or visibility returns the existing photo, conflicts, or modifies it.
open_points.question: What happens when a PhotoPublication repeats an existing `intake_id` with content different from the stored ProgressPhoto?
options: Return the existing photo regardless of differing content
Treat differing content as an integrity conflict and change nothing
Apply some differing fields as an update to the existing photo
open_points.default_guess: Treat different content as an integrity conflict and change nothing.

witness.initial: Photo F exists from `intake_id = I`, with file reference X and caption `before`.
events: Authorized staff publishes `intake_id = I` again with file reference Y and caption `after`.
outcomes: The operation reports replay and returns F unchanged.
The operation reports an integrity conflict.
F is changed to use some or all of the new publication facts.
witness.observer: The publishing staff member and later gallery readers see different operation results or photo content.

open_points.subject: Meaning of ProgressPhoto client visibility on reads
open_points.text: M35 says staff can change `client_visible` and refers to `hiding a photo`, while PhotoView omits `client_visible`; the texts do not state whether a hidden photo is omitted from a viewer's gallery entirely or remains listed with only its binary inaccessible.
open_points.question: For a ClientViewer, does `client_visible = false` hide the entire ProgressPhoto from gallery reads, or only prohibit its binary download?
options: Exclude the photo from viewer gallery results and refuse its binary
Include its metadata in the viewer gallery but refuse its binary
open_points.default_guess: Exclude the photo from the viewer gallery and refuse its binary.

witness.initial: Viewer V has access to project P; photo F in P is initially client-visible.
events: Authorized staff changes F to `client_visible = false`.
outcomes: F is absent from the gallery.
F remains in the gallery with date, caption, and section, but its binary cannot be downloaded.
witness.observer: The ClientViewer sees whether hidden-photo metadata remains visible.

open_points.subject: Audit of first-administrator bootstrap
open_points.text: R0-07 says the bootstrap command is `never printed, logged or audited`, while M36 says `The first-administrator bootstrap of R0-07 is no exception: it writes one staff.create record with actor kind system`.
open_points.question: Does successful first-administrator bootstrap create an AuditRecord?
options: Create no audit record, as R0-07 requires
Create exactly one system `staff.create` AuditRecord, as M36 requires
open_points.default_guess: Create the M36 system audit record because it is the later model-specific statement, while flagging the unresolved contradiction.

witness.initial: A fresh deployment has no StaffAccount and no AuditRecord.
events: The host operator successfully runs the local bootstrap command to create administrator A.
An authorized audit reader or database inspection reads audit history.
outcomes: No audit entry exists for the bootstrap.
One successful system `staff.create` entry names A's `staff_id`.
witness.observer: An administrator, auditor, or deployment operator inspecting audit history sees the difference.
